title: COMP 4736 · Part 3
subtitle: Processes: the model, creation and termination, states and transitions, the process table and context switch, modeling multiprogramming, Linux processes, zombies and orphans
description: Part 3 of Rahim Oraji's lectures (Tanenbaum Ch. 2): a process as a program in execution with its three segments, multiprogramming as rapid switching, the four creation events and four termination conditions, UNIX process groups against Windows handles, the three states and four numbered transitions, the process table entry and the context switch into the PCB, the interrupt skeleton and vector, CPU utilization = 1 − pⁿ with the 80 % / 10-process example, then Linux: the address space, fork() with pids 4508 and 4509, the stripped-down shell, /proc, pstree, ps and top, the ps state letters D I R S T X Z, the Linux state diagram, zombies and orphans. Playback animations for the state transitions, the context switch and fork; a utilization calculator with the RAM-budget and parallel-jobs modes the written midterm uses. Ends with a mock midterm section and the closed-book recall drill.
intro:
:::quiz Midterm weight
On the instructor's practice paper this Part carries 11 of the 74 Part 1 marks and three of the five written questions (CPU utilization from a job timeline, 1 − pⁿ with a RAM budget, two parallel jobs with I/O wait). The written questions are arithmetic you must show on paper: utilization = CPU busy ÷ total time, 1 − pⁿ, n = (RAM − OS) ÷ process size. Closed book, so every definition and list here must come from memory.
:::
